title: Reading a real brief, and writing one that is not trivial

videos.script: Every real project starts with somebody describing a problem badly. Not because they are careless, but because they know their problem and not yours. {{badly}} A brief is what turns that description into something you can build and check. It says what the problem is, who has it, what must happen, what must never happen, and when it is done. {{parts}} loanbook started with a message like that. What it left out, and the questions that filled the gaps, became the brief the rest of the course builds against. Then it asks what makes a brief worth building at all, because a brief can be perfectly clear and still describe something trivial.
